concepts.why: The presence of multiple angiofibromas, conical teeth, and a history of renal transplant at a young age, along with the histologic and electron microscopy findings, are consistent with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.

The combination of angiofibromas, conical teeth, and a history of renal disease could be suggestive of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1, although the absence of other endocrine tumors and the specific histologic findings make this less likely.

The presence of skin-colored papules and conical teeth could be seen in Focal Dermal Hypoplasia, but the lack of other characteristic features such as fat herniations and the specific histologic findings make this diagnosis less likely.

rationales.F01: Facial papules are a common feature of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
rationales.F02: Multiple facial papules are consistent with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
rationales.F03: Absence of hypopigmented macules, periungual fibromas, or Shagreen plaques does not rule out Tuberous Sclerosis Complex but makes other diagnoses less likely.
rationales.F04: Conical teeth can be associated with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
rationales.F05: Histologic findings of angiofibroma are characteristic of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
rationales.F07: Crystalline inclusions within dermal fibroblasts are a distinctive feature of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of skin-colored, dome-shaped firm papules over the chin, nose, and perinasal region, dozens of skin-colored dome-shaped papules over the chin, nasal, and perinasal regions of the face, and several teeth with a conical shape are all consistent with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex. The histologic analysis showing a dome-shaped lesion with several plump fibroblasts and increased blood vessels, compatible with an angiofibroma, further supports this diagnosis.
